reason: E1 shows that ultrathin ALD layers suppress interdiffusion and suggests nitrides could be better, directly supporting the barrier concept. E2 and E3 confirm Cr-coated Zr cladding is promising and that Cr–Zr interdiffusion is critical, but neither provides evidence for a nitride barrier in this specific nuclear application. The key premise that a nitride barrier will work under the extreme conditions (1100 °C steam, irradiation) is not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Nanometer-thick ALD layers can suppress metal interdiffusion up to 600 °C
Nitrides may perform even better as diffusion barriers than Al2O3
Cr-coated Zr cladding is a promising EATF concept with good adhesion and oxidation resistance
Cr–Zr interdiffusion at the interface significantly affects coating performance
